summary: Woerden (province of Utrecht) charges for on-street parking in four tariff zones (4400, 4401, 4403, 4404). Under the parking tax ordinance adopted by the council on 27 November 2025 and in force from 1 January 2026, zones 4400, 4401 and 4404 cost 0.32 euros per 6 minutes (3.20 euros an hour), with maximum stays of 180, 30 and 120 minutes, and zone 4403 costs 6.20 euros an hour up to 24.80 euros a day. A decision of the mayor and aldermen of 9 December 2025 sets paid hours at Monday to Saturday 10:00 to 18:30, and until 22:00 in zone 4403. The 2026 table lists a first residents' permit at 240.20 euros and a second at 480.40 euros (the period is not stated in the published table), and the decision caps permits per zone, with a stated total of 790 permits on 844 spaces (the zone rows add up to more than 844, so that total is not fully reliable). The published terms for the Castellum garage set short-stay parking at 2.50 euros an hour on Monday to Saturday from 08:00 to 18:30, free on evenings from 18:30 to 22:00 and on Sundays, with a day ticket of 18.60 euros and a 777 euro full subscription from 1 April 2026; the terms for the Defensie-eiland garage repeat the same figures but are evidently copied from the Castellum terms, so they should be treated with caution. Q-Park runs the P+R Spoorlaan (172 spaces, open 24 hours, plate recognition); its tariff did not load, and no source links it to the 'P+R Noord' that the municipality mentions. The municipality's plans for parking regulation south of the station rest on a 2025 process: the public input summary of 2 June 2025 counted 475 ideas and comments (248 for Stationsgebied/Hoofdstedenbuurt, 56 for Nieuw-Middelland, 41 for Snellerpoort), with keeping parking free the most frequent opinion, and the FAQ and reply note (undated, apparently from 2025) say 3,500 to 5,000 homes will be built over 10 to 15 years with low parking norms and parking on private land. The municipality says it wants the P+R Zuid site regulated while investigating keeping it free for rail travellers. Whether the council took a decision on the extension, and any utilisation statistics, could not be established. The Omgevingsvisie, adopted in 2022 and republished on 21 January 2026, aims at a car-light town centre, more regulated parking areas and lower parking norms for new development.

items.text: The council adopted the Parking Tax Ordinance 2026 on 27 November 2025, in force from 1 January 2026. Paid zones 4400, 4401 and 4404 cost 0.32 euros per 6 minutes (3.20 euros an hour) with maximum stays of 180, 30 and 120 minutes; zone 4403 costs 6.20 euros an hour up to 24.80 euros a day.
items.source_title: Verordening op de heffing en de invordering van parkeerbelastingen 2026 (Woerden)

items.text: The mayor and aldermen decided on 9 December 2025 (published in the municipal gazette on 30 December 2025) that paid parking applies Monday to Saturday 10:00-18:30 in zones 4400, 4401 and 4404 and 10:00-22:00 in zone 4403. Payment is made in advance by giving the area code to a parking service provider by phone (or another method the provider accepts), or by electronic means (debit or credit card, NFC) at the parking machine. The decision replaces the earlier 'Nadere voorschriften parkeren 2024' decision (adopted 18 March 2025) and takes effect the day after publication.
items.source_title: Gemeenteblad 2025, 571510: Nadere voorschriften parkeren gemeente Woerden 2026

items.text: Prices in the 2026 tariff table: first residents' permit 240.20 euros, second residents' permit 480.40 euros, business permit 906.80 euros and commuter permit 240.20 euros (the published table header does not state the period, so a yearly price is not confirmed). Visitor parking costs 0.32 euros an hour (paid per minute) with a ceiling of 96 euros per calendar year. A work-parking day permit costs 18 euros and the penalty charge (naheffingsaanslag) is 82 euros.
items.source_title: Verordening op de heffing en de invordering van parkeerbelastingen 2026 (Woerden)

items.text: Permits are capped per zone: the 2026 decision lists 844 permit-zone spaces, with a ceiling of 790 permits (94 percent) and at most 57 second permits. The commuter permit is valid only in Oostsingel and Oostlaan, and residents of zones 4400 and 4401 who hold a Castellum or Defensie-eiland garage subscription cannot also get a first residents' or business permit.
items.source_title: Gemeenteblad 2025, 571510: Nadere voorschriften parkeren gemeente Woerden 2026

items.text: The terms for the Castellum garage (Meulmansweg 8), effective 1 January 2026, set short-stay parking at 2.50 euros an hour Monday to Saturday 08:00-18:30, 1.25 euros an hour Monday to Thursday 22:00-24:00, and free on evenings 18:30-22:00, nights and Sundays. A day ticket costs 18.60 euros, the garage is open 24 hours, and the owner may index prices yearly.
items.source_title: Gemeenteblad 2025, 570832: Algemene Voorwaarden Parkeergarage Castellum Woerden, januari 2026

items.text: Castellum subscriptions from 1 April 2026: full subscription 777 euros a year, off-peak subscription 518 euros, residents' subscription 206 euros with a ceiling of 220 residents' subscriptions and a waiting list above that. The terms name Coöperatie ParkeerService U.A. as the website where they are published.
items.source_title: Gemeenteblad 2025, 570832: Algemene Voorwaarden Parkeergarage Castellum Woerden, januari 2026

items.text: The terms for the Defensie-eiland garage, also effective 1 January 2026, carry the same short-stay tariff as Castellum (2.50 euros an hour by day, free evenings and Sundays, day ticket 18.60 euros) and the same 777 euro full and 206 euro residents' subscription prices from April 2026. The document's definitions section still names the Castellum address, so the text appears copied from the Castellum terms.
items.source_title: Gemeenteblad 2025, 571228: Algemene Voorwaarden Parkeergarage Defensie-eiland Woerden, januari 2026

items.text: Q-Park lists a single Woerden site, P+R Spoorlaan (3445 AE), with 172 spaces, open 24 hours on all days, licence-plate recognition, bicycle parking and disabled bays. Its tariff widget did not load when the page was read on 21 October 2026.

The municipality's project page on extending parking regulation south of the station (read 21 October 2026; the content appears to date from 2025, for example it mentions a feedback round 'before Christmas' and a provisional planning) says homes will be built over the next 15 years close to the bus and train station, and that Snellerpoort will have fewer public parking spaces. It names high parking pressure at the P&R Houttuinlaan, with parkers using neighbouring residential and business areas, and spill-over from Snellerpoort into adjacent areas such as Stationsgebied/Hoofdstedenbuurt, as reasons for extra rules south of the station. Working groups are set up for Nieuw-Middelland, Stationsgebied-Zuid/Hoofdstedenbuurt and Snellerpoort.

The FAQ on the same project page (undated, read 21 October 2026, referring to a 2025 process) says paid parking, if chosen, would follow the town-centre rules and that the council policy is to make neither profit nor loss. The FAQ adds that the council decided for now not to start on the fringe areas around the old town north of the railway, which the 2024 starting note had also named.
items.source_title: Veelgestelde vragen over uitbreiding parkeerregulering (gemeente Woerden)

items.text: The Nota van opbrengsten (summary of public input, dated 2 June 2025) counted 475 ideas and comments submitted between 4 February and 3 March 2025, mostly through an online map tool: 248 for Stationsgebied/Hoofdstedenbuurt, 56 for Nieuw-Middelland, 41 for Snellerpoort, 103 'elsewhere' and 27 'other'. The most frequently voiced opinion was to keep parking free. The municipality expected the council to decide on parking regulation in early October 2025; the page does not report any decision and none was found.
items.source_title: Nota van opbrengsten uitbreiding parkeerregulering (gemeente Woerden)

items.text: In the reply note (undated; the public page summarising the most frequent questions, read 21 October 2026) the municipality says it considers it important that the P&R Zuid site is regulated so that parkers from the surrounding new homes do not use it, while also wanting it to remain usable by public-transport travellers. It is investigating whether parking for travellers can stay free, using the system at P&R Noord as an example; the conditions are stated on Q-Park's website. It says new-build residents must park on their own land under lower parking norms in Nieuw-Middelland, Snellerpoort and Stationsgebied, and that it currently has no plans to create extra public parking spaces.

The municipality's traffic page (read 21 October 2026) states the parking vision: fewer cars on the street especially in the centre, garages preferred, and residential parking mainly for residents. It also lists the Traffic Vision 2030 and a charging vision.

The Omgevingsvisie was adopted by the municipal council on 9 June 2022; the mayor and aldermen decided on 20 January 2026 to make it available on the digital Omgevingsloket, and it was published in the municipal gazette on 21 January 2026. As written in 2022, it aims at a car-light town centre, extension of the areas with regulated parking and lower parking norms for new development if set conditions are met. It also planned, as of 2022, to build the Rembrandtbrug in 2026, to close the Polanertunnel to cars in both directions once the alternative is ready, and to work out P&R sites regionally from 2022.

Nieuw-Middelland projects listed by the municipality (read 21 October 2026): 134 homes at Watermolenlaan 1 and 132 homes at Watermolenlaan 4/Houttuinlaan 5, both expected to start building in 2026, 59 homes at Zaagmolenhof 4, and 285 rental homes at Houttuinlaan 6-12 with construction starting at the end of 2027.

The municipal page on the sewer in Houttuinlaan (read 21 October 2026) says the two new housing schemes in Nieuw-Middelland, at Watermolenlaan 4/Houttuinlaan 5 (132 homes) and Watermolenlaan 1 (134 homes), will each have a half-sunken parking cellar, that Watermolenlaan is closed from 21 September for the whole construction period, and that works for a sewer bypass in the Houttuinlaan at the level of parking garage De Houttuin start on 19 October 2026, with the street closed for 4 weeks. Work on the main sewer was postponed and is due to restart in 2027.

The municipal page for requesting charge points (undated, read 21 October 2026) says that at the end of 'this year' (the year is not stated on the page) the municipality will place charge points on the basis of data: expected growth of electric cars per neighbourhood, use of existing charge points and the possibilities on location. Residents then no longer need to apply, but can report a missing charge point; where no charge point exists they can apply through Park&Charge. The page also says the number of charge points will be expanded in the coming years.

gaps: Council information system (gemeenteraad.woerden.nl, secure-woerden.gemeenteoplossingen.nl) returned HTTP 503 (offline for maintenance) on 21 October 2026, so none of its papers could be read: raadsinformatiebrief Stand van zaken diverse parkeerdossiers July 2025, raadsvoorstel belastingverordeningen 2026 (3.5 percent indexation), Q&A budget committee on parking Nov 2025, startnotitie uitbreiding parkeerregulering 2024, laadvisie, parkeervisie.
The final council decision on extended parking regulation in Poort van Woerden (expected October 2025) and any later introduction date or tariffs for P+R Zuid were not found.

Zone maps (which streets belong to zones 4400, 4401, 4403, 4404) are attachments (Bijlage 1-7) not extracted; zone 4403 tariff of 6.20 euros an hour was read from the ordinance table but its streets and rationale are not confirmed.
woerden.parkeerservice.nl returned 403 and was not worked around; Parkeerservice tariffs, bezoekersregeling and permit pages unread.
nieuw-middelland.nl and snellerpoort.nl returned 503; q-park.nl P+R Spoorlaan tariff widget did not load; no 2026 P+R tariff found.
centrumparkeren.nl was not used because it is a parking-listing portal; its figures (e.g. 520 spaces in Castellum, 80 in Defensie-eiland, 1.69 euros an hour at P+R) are unverified.
The Gemeenteblad 2024, 229848 charging policy page named the municipality of Oudewater in its text, so it was not used.

No utilisation statements (occupancy of garages or P+R) found in sources opened; the July 2025 letter said to mention 17 of 18 Defensie-eiland subscriptions was only seen in a search summary and is not cited.
No source found on EV charging in the garages, a parking guidance system, or open data from Woerden; web search budget was exhausted so no local press (Woerdense Courant, Indebuurt, AD) was reviewed.
